items.description: 19 of the 20 spec deltas (every change except toolkit-consistency) are plan-roadmap scaffolds whose scenarios are circular: `WHEN <change-id> is implemented THEN <acceptance outcome>`. Each SHALL technically has a WHEN/THEN, but none is verifiable, and all sit under the placeholder capability `multiplayer-collaboration`, for which no `openspec/specs/` directory exists. toolkit-consistency's own plan-findings graded this same pattern 'critical testability' and replaced it. Acceptable as scaffolds that /plan-feature or PLAN_ITERATE must refine, but they must not pass through to IMPLEMENT as-is.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: The scaffold generator truncates requirement headings mid-sentence with `...` and lowercases the first character of the outcome, producing `pRs created by` here (and `that given any`, `that /implement-feature` elsewhere). `### Requirement:` headings are the identity used by opsx:sync and by the planned requirement-level collision scanner (ri-06), so truncated, near-identical headings undermine the very collision detection this roadmap introduces.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: The rationale for `proposal_approval: auto` is that a recorded `roadmap_approval` already authorizes the plans inside a roadmap. But `proposal_approval` also fires for standalone changes started via /plan-feature or /autopilot with no parent roadmap, where no roadmap_approval exists. As written, the posture removes the only human intent gate for non-roadmap changes, which contradicts the epic's own P3 (intent is an owned artifact) and the fail-closed constraint.
items.resolution: operator disposition 2026-10-10: implemented elsewhere (ri-21 dispatch-contract #667, main 731557b)

items.description: The header comment says 'every failure/escalation path still wait[s] for a human', but `replan_required` (fires when a roadmap item enters `replan_required`, i.e. after a failed plan) is set to `auto`. The table further down is internally consistent (`proposal_approval, replan_required | auto`), so only the comment is wrong, but the comment is what an operator reads first.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: Two operator approvals of `escalate_resume` cite a 'cloud single-vendor review policy (TRUST_POSTURE.md 479dcd9)' as their authority. The TRUST_POSTURE.md in this packet contains no review-quorum or single-vendor policy at all; it only defines gate dispositions. Either the policy lives in a commit not present here, or the authority citation is unverifiable from the repository, which defeats P9 traceability. Both approvals also carry `approval_id: null`, so the only record of the human decision is free text in `reason`.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: Canonical roadmap state disagrees with the change loop-state. `toolkit-consistency/loop-state.json` shows ri-20 ran GATEKEEPER and PLAN_ITERATE on 2026-10-05 and has been parked in PLAN_REVIEW twice, yet roadmap.yaml still lists ri-20 as `approved` (not `in_progress`), checkpoint.json has no dispatch_attempt for it, `current_item_id` is still ri-01, and roadmap `status` is `planning` after a recorded roadmap_approval proceed. Per docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md roadmap.yaml/loop-state.json are the canonical state a rebuilt queue is projected from, so a reconciliation would re-dispatch ri-20 as fresh work.
items.resolution: operator disposition 2026-10-10: owned by roadmap supervisor bookkeeping pass

items.description: The dispatch handshake `launch_token` and lease `owner_nonce` are committed in a tracked file. They appear to be single-use and already consumed (lease state `released`, gate `entered`), so exposure is low, but committing live-looking tokens trains readers to treat them as harmless and will trip secret scanners.
items.resolution: operator disposition 2026-10-10: accepted; checkpoint digest-only since 4955e24

items.description: The One-way consumption requirement says merged shared records 'SHALL participate in the existing deduplication', and design.md states that dedupe key is `(capability_gap, affected_skill, session_id)`. But the Exported learning privacy requirement drops `session_id` and allowlists only `event_type, summary, outcome, lessons, tags, created_at`, so neither `session_id` nor top-level `capability_gap`/`affected_skill` exist on an exported record. The exporter's own dedupe key `(capability_gap, affected_skill, summary)` likewise uses two fields that are not in the allowlist. The two requirements cannot both hold unless capability_gap/affected_skill are recovered from tags and the consumer dedupe key is changed.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): spec.md Exported learning privacy names capability_gap/affected_skill as retained tag values; One-way consumption dedupes shared records on (capability_gap, affected_skill, summary).

items.description: The privacy requirement drops the `agent_id` and `session_id` fields but exports `tags` verbatim. Per docs/guides/memory-conventions.md, memory entries are tagged with identifiers such as `agent:<id>`, `session:<id>`, `change:<id>` and vendor/model tags, so the identity the allowlist removes re-enters through tags. The secret sanitizer targets credential patterns, not identifiers, so it will not catch this. No scenario covers tag-encoded identity.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): spec.md tags filtered to D4 namespaces; identity/context tags dropped; scenario 'Identity-bearing tags are dropped' added.

items.description: Because the stamp is the pin (D3) and every successful install overwrites it, a teammate who runs install.sh from an un-pinned toolkit checkout silently moves the team's pin instead of hitting drift. The drift check only runs under `--check`. No scenario covers 'install over an existing stamp whose hash differs from the new source', so the implementation is free to overwrite without even a notice; the only safeguard is a git diff on a hash string.

plan-findings.md and session-log.md both claim 25 scenarios; the spec delta contains 26 (Install stamp 4, Payload hash 4, Drift check 6, Shared learnings opt-in 3, Exported learning privacy 4, One-way consumption 3, State-artifact registration 2).
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): plan-findings.md scenario count corrected (26, 27 after finding 9); Iteration 2 section added.

items.description: The record's `written_at` (06:59:55.764) is 35 ms earlier than the `decided_at` of the decision it contains (06:59:55.799), so the file claims to have been written before the decision it records. Two different timestamp formats (`+00:00` vs `Z`) are also used in the same file.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: Priority inversion: ri-13 (priority 2) depends on ri-12 (priority 3), so the priority-2 item cannot become ready until a priority-3 item completes. Under the autopilot-roadmap/queue ordering the priority field then misrepresents effective scheduling order.

items.description: The Install stamp and Drift check requirements use `<target-root>` for the consumer repository while the Shared learnings and One-way consumption requirements use `<project-root>` for the same directory. Readers may infer two different roots (install target vs the project the exporter runs in).
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): spec.md uses <target-root> consistently and defines it once.

items.description: After the operator-approved resume, `escalation_reason` still holds the pre-resume reason, `previous_phase` equals `current_phase`, and `iteration` is 0 while `total_iterations` is 8. Readers of the loop-state cannot tell whether the loop is still escalated or running. Harmless for execution but reduces the state file's value as the canonical record.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: Scaffold proposals list dependencies as roadmap item IDs (`ri-02`) rather than change IDs (`ownership-map`). A change proposal is meant to be readable on its own in a PR; a reader without the roadmap cannot resolve `ri-02`. This matters more given the epic's constraint that artifacts stay legible to teammates who do not use the skills.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: Review fixes 9 (tag-namespace filtering) and 14 (`<project-root>` → `<target-root>`) were applied to spec.md only. The planning artifacts implementers actually follow still describe the pre-fix behaviour: tasks.md T5 defaults `--shared-learnings` to `<project-root>/.agentic-toolkit/learnings.jsonl`; tasks.md T4 and design.md D8 say records carry `tags` with no mention of filtering to the `failure_type:`/`capability_gap:`/`affected_skill:`/`severity:`/`source:` namespaces; proposal.md 'What Changes' §4 likewise lists `tags` verbatim in the allowlist. An implementer working from tasks.md would ship the identity leak the spec now forbids and would reintroduce the two-roots ambiguity.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX round 2 (conductor, inline): tasks.md T4/T5, design.md D8 and proposal.md item 4 now carry the tag-namespace filter, the (capability_gap, affected_skill, summary) dedupe key and <target-root>.

items.description: The Exported learning privacy requirement ends with 'The exporter SHALL pass the Cross-Repo Portability gate' but has no scenario for it; the only portability scenario in the delta is under Payload hash and covers `payload_hash.py`, not `export_shared_learnings.py`. plan-findings.md row 8 claims 'portability scenarios under Payload hash and Exported learning privacy', so the ledger over-reports coverage. Either add a scenario (e.g. WHEN `validate_install_manifest.py` and the consumer-portability test run after the exporter is added THEN they pass and the exporter is listed in `smoke_entrypoints`) or move the SHALL into Payload hash's scenario.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX round 2 (conductor, inline): scenario 'Exporter passes the portability gate' added under Exported learning privacy.

items.description: One-way consumption has three SHALLs without a scenario: accepting `--shared-learnings <path>` (no scenario with a non-default path), deduplicating merged records on `(capability_gap, affected_skill, summary)` against local and other shared findings (no scenario where a shared record duplicates a local one and appears once), and the behaviour when an exported record lacks a `capability_gap:` or `affected_skill:` tag, which leaves the dedupe key partially undefined for both exporter and consumer.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX round 2 (conductor, inline): scenario 'Duplicate shared record appears once' (explicit path + dedupe); missing gap tags map to 'unknown' as in analyze_failures.py.

items.description: Ledger item 16 (file_path `openspec/changes/owner-routed-escalation/proposal.md`) carries a `spec_file` that is (a) an absolute path into this agent's private worktree (`/home/user/agentic-coding-tools/.claude/worktrees/agent-a2592d0f7287ff5d2/...`) and (b) points at toolkit-consistency's spec, which the finding is not about. Every other item uses repo-relative paths. A committed machine-local path breaks the ledger for any other checkout and the mis-association would mislead a spec-level fingerprint match in later rounds.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX round 2 (conductor, inline): item 16 spec_file cleared (absolute worktree path pointing at the wrong spec).

items.description: The summary table asserts that `pr_creation` 'Fails closed if the notification is undelivered', but the Dispositions section, which is the normative description of `notify_with_timeout`, defines only 'file approval, notify, poll until timeout, apply default_action' and says nothing about undelivered notifications. With `default_action: proceed` the documented semantics would proceed after an hour regardless of delivery. Either document the undelivered-notification rule under Dispositions or drop the claim from the table so the contract does not promise behaviour it does not specify.
items.resolution: IMPL_REVIEW 2026-10-10: file outside toolkit-consistency; tabled to owner in plan-findings.md Iteration 2 (PLAN_REVIEW decision 4)

items.description: Iteration 2 cites `.review-cache/round-1/review-manifest.json` as dispatch evidence for the single-vendor degradation, but that file is not part of the committed packet (only `.review-ledger/ledger.json` is). The vendor-availability evidence for the min_quorum=1 decision is therefore not reproducible from git, which is the same P9 traceability gap ledger item 5 raises for the policy citation. Either commit the manifest or summarise its contents in plan-findings.md.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX round 2 (conductor, inline): plan-findings.md cites .review-cache/round-1-initial/; manifest, findings, fact-check and raw meta committed for both runs.
